clue.text: Meat business stifled by embargo

indicators.note: something stifled is smothered, so the word for business is held inside the embargo word

parts.note: an embargo is a ban on trade
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A meat trader has been choked off by a trade embargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is cured pig meat, an example of meat.

clue.text: Hang scabbard here? This is unfair

definitions.meaning: a sword's sheath hangs beneath a belt at the waist
a boxing foul struck beneath the waistline, hence unfair

explanation.surface: A place to hang one's sword is deemed unsporting.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing blow struck beneath the waistband is illegal, giving the idiom for unfair tactics.

clue.text: Goods carried originally by legendary vessel

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the word, its first letter

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek legend

explanation.surface: Goods were first carried by a mythical ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the freight a ship carries, the goods aboard.

clue.text: It's inevitable, what wine-making does

definitions.meaning: from '... when the devil drives', said when there is no choice
wine-making requires grape juice, called must

explanation.surface: Wine-making is unavoidable.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says one must act when forced to, and wine production requires the unfermented grape juice called must.

clue.text: Tonic indicated by thumb

definitions.meaning: a tonic is a restorative drink that revives you
a hitchhiker's raised thumb asks passing drivers for a lift

explanation.surface: A medicine is recommended by a thumbs-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A restorative drink is a reviving tonic, and a hitchhiker's thumb asks drivers to stop and give a lift.

clue.text: Potash has been dispersed — a cause for pity

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Spilt potash is a sad sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The stored clue borrowed words from 12 Across; the page prints 'a cause for pity'. 'has been dispersed' rearranges POTASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality in something that arouses pity or sorrow.

clue.text: Crazy, what overheated kiln may do?

definitions.meaning: an eccentric or mad person, used adjectivally
too much heat in a kiln may split a pot

explanation.surface: An overheated kiln goes mad.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric person is a crank, and a pottery kiln run too hot may split a pot.

clue.text: Whisky delivered to a seagirt republic

parts.note: malt is malt whisky

explanation.surface: Whisky is shipped to an island state.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is a Mediterranean island republic, surrounded by sea.

clue.text: Deprived of status and given no food, devouring confectionery

indicators.note: the hungry word swallows the sweet, holding it inside

parts.note: unfed means not given food
rock is a hard stick sweet sold at British seaside resorts

explanation.surface: Someone stripped of rank and starved eats sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest unfrocked is stripped of clerical office, so deprived of status.

clue.text: Lean girl — her fat dreadfully exaggerated

indicators.note: done dreadfully, the letters of these four words are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thin girl is horribly distorted in thinking herself fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadfully' scrambles the fourteen letters of LEAN GIRL HER FAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bigger than real life is overblown, a synonym for exaggerated.

clue.text: Mean character, a petty thief?

definitions.meaning: someone who pinches, steals, mere pennies

explanation.surface: A miserly character is a small-time thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser is called by this idiom, and literally one who pinches small coins would be a petty thief.

clue.text: Log pile found near Oxford

parts.note: a log is a piece of wood
a pile is a stock or supply laid up

explanation.surface: A heap of logs has been discovered close to Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: WOODSTOCK is an Oxfordshire town, home of Blenheim Palace, a few miles north of Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxfordshire town lies a few miles north of the university city, so it is a place found nearby.

clue.text: A note in harmony

clue.text: Minor problem, setback for composer dropping in on Henry

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: a setback sends something back, so the trimmed composer is read backwards
dropping means the word in is let fall from the composer's name

parts.note: Puccini was the Italian opera composer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer suffers a small reverse when Henry drops in on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on Henry' puts the composer's remnant after H, the physics symbol, which the surface hides behind a visitor called Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: A small snag or temporary setback is called a hiccup in idiom.

clue.text: Look after tea for each person

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
per means for each
one means a person

explanation.surface: Tea is served for every individual in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaperone is to escort and look after someone, typically a young person.

clue.text: Left because of wriggling snake …

parts.note: for can mean because of, as in 'jumped for joy'

indicators.note: a wriggling thing twists about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was abandoned on account of a writhing serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsaken means abandoned, a synonym for left behind.

clue.text: Political leader says piece

parts.note: states means says
a man is a piece in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A politician speaks as a token figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A statesman is an experienced political leader.

clue.text: Crack in a certain vessel …

parts.note: one can mean a certain, as in 'one Mr Smith'
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A crack has appeared in a particular ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a joke or quip, and a short single joke is a quip.

clue.text: … showing off, snake means to inject poison

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake
a sting is the means by which a wasp or scorpion injects venom

explanation.surface: A snake shows off its venomous weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Bragging about oneself is showing off, a close synonym.

clue.text: Fully committed to help feeding dog

indicators.note: the help word feeds into the dog word, going inside it

parts.note: a pup is a young dog
aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone is wholly dedicated to helping feed a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A paid-up member is fully committed to a cause, an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: … and other things he had engraved

parts.note: etc. abbreviates et cetera, and other things
he'd is the contraction of he had

explanation.surface: Someone engraved further items.
explanation.definitionFit: Etched means engraved by acid on metal or glass.

clue.text: One doing sponging for old doctor

definitions.meaning: a sponger who lives off others like a bloodsucking worm
an archaic word for a physician

explanation.surface: A freeloader stands in for a doctor of former times.
explanation.definitionFit: The bloodsucking worm gives a word for a parasite, and it was also an old name for a physician.

clue.text: Indian has the measure of the Israelites, and of the French

parts.note: the hin was an ancient Hebrew liquid measure
du is French for of the

explanation.surface: An Indian holds an ancient Hebrew measure and a French one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu is a follower of Hinduism, the majority religion of India.

clue.text: Container for rubbish made in brittle material

indicators.note: read as a verb-like signal, the letters are made into new material, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rubbish receptacle is made of fragile stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: The stored clue lost its last word; the page prints 'material'. IN and BRITTLE are reshaped, with 'made ... material' signalling it.
explanation.definitionFit: A street receptacle for discarded rubbish is a container for rubbish, a literal description.

clue.text: Confined to vault

explanation.surface: Someone is restricted to a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Bound means tied up or restricted, and as a noun it is a leap.

clue.text: Blue feathers, orally

parts.note: down is soft fine feathers
orally means by way of the mouth

explanation.surface: Blue plumage is described in terms of the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Being glum or depressed is feeling blue, an idiom for sadness.

clue.text: Needed a lot of papers in colour

indicators.note: the papers word sits inside the colour word

parts.note: red is a colour
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Many coloured documents were needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Required means needed, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Drain off into the depths

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: Water is drained away into deep places.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest point of anything is its nadir, the depths of a situation.
